title: Word Break II
summary: Given a string and a dictionary of words, insert spaces into the string to form sentences where each word is in the dictionary.
statement: Given a string and a dictionary of words, insert spaces into the string to form sentences where each word is in the dictionary. Return all possible sentences in any order, allowing words in the dictionary to be reused.
constraints: s has 1–20 lowercase letters. The dictionary contains 1–1000 distinct lowercase words, each 1–10 letters long.
Return every complete segmentation as a sentence with single spaces between words and no leading/trailing space. Word reuse is allowed; answer order is unrestricted.
The source guarantees answer length at most 100000. Do not return duplicate sentences, a partial prefix, or only the first valid answer.
hints: Choosing a dictionary prefix leaves a smaller instance: all sentences for the remaining suffix.
Use recursive suffix solving with memoization by starting position.
For each matching next word, prepend it to every sentence from the suffix. At the end return one empty suffix so completed words form a sentence.
Add a space only when the suffix is nonempty. Cache suffix results, but do not stop after the first successful branch.
editorial: Recursively enumerate matching next words and combine each with every sentence available from its suffix. Caching by the starting index avoids solving identical suffixes repeatedly. The base case is a list containing an empty string, representing one completed choice, not an empty list representing failure. Depth is at most 20. Output generation can be exponential and must be included in complexity: if C is total text held across cached suffix sentences, the reference takes O(nL² + C + dictionary characters) time and O(C+n+dictionary characters) storage. The independent oracle enumerates cut masks, not recursive suffix combinations.

tests.explanation: Two splits work: cats|and|dog and cat|sand|dog, producing two complete sentences.
The three sentences are pine apple pen apple, pineapple pen apple, and pine applepen apple; each covers the full string.

expected: aa aa aa aa aa aa aa aa aa aa
